branches.name: branches
branches.description: Physical bank branches. Generated first — all other collections that reference a branch use branch_id from this collection.

manager_id.note: Integrity rule: manager must be an employee whose branch_id equals this branch_id

status.note: v2: lowercase; expanded to include inactive and closed for edge-case testing

relationships.description: Manager must work at this same branch — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Manager must work at this same branch — see data_integrity_rules

employees.name: employees
employees.description: Bank staff. Referenced by branches (manager), customers (relationship_manager), accounts (account_manager), loans (loan_officer), kyc_documents (verified_by), support_tickets (assigned_agent), and fraud_alerts (reviewed_by).

designation.note: role_level field removed in v2 — use designation for seniority

relationships.description: Each employee belongs to one branch

merchants.name: merchants
merchants.description: Registered merchants where customers make purchases. Referenced by transactions.merchant_id (nullable — null for cash/NEFT/internal transfers).

customers.name: customers
customers.description: Bank customers (individual and corporate). Central entity — referenced by every other domain collection.

status.note: v2: lowercase — matches every other collection

accounts.name: accounts
accounts.description: Bank accounts. A customer can have zero, one, or multiple accounts. Referenced by transactions and cards.

relationships.description: One customer can have multiple accounts

transactions.name: transactions
transactions.description: Financial transactions. Largest collection (~10k). customer_id is denormalised and must always equal accounts[account_id].customer_id.

customer_id.note: Denormalised — enforced equal to accounts[account_id].customer_id by generator

is_flagged.description: True for ~2% of transactions; fraud_alerts reference these

relationships.description: Denormalised — enforced equal to accounts.customer_id for this account

cards.name: cards
cards.description: Debit and credit cards. customer_id MUST match accounts[account_id].customer_id (enforced by generator). Expired cards have status='expired'.

customer_id.note: Derived from account_id — must equal accounts[account_id].customer_id

relationships.description: Must match the customer of cards.account_id — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Must match the customer of cards.account_id — see data_integrity_rules

loans.name: loans
loans.description: Loan records. Null-field rules: closed → outstanding=0, next_due=null; defaulted → next_due in past; active → next_due in future.

outstanding_amount.description: Remaining balance. 0 when status=closed; >0 when active or defaulted

next_due_date.note: Null when status=closed. Past date when defaulted. Future date when active.

kyc_documents.name: kyc_documents
kyc_documents.description: KYC identity documents. verification_status != 'verified' → verified_by and verification_date must both be null.

support_tickets.name: support_tickets
support_tickets.description: Customer support tickets. status not in ('resolved','closed') → resolved_date, resolution_notes, satisfaction_rating are all null.

fraud_alerts.name: fraud_alerts
fraud_alerts.description: Fraud alerts derived from flagged transactions. customer_id is always derived from transaction→account→customer chain — never independently assigned.

relationships.description: Derived from transaction→account→customer chain — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Derived from transaction→account→customer chain — see data_integrity_rules

investments.name: investments
investments.description: Customer investment portfolio. investment_type='stocks' → maturity_date=null. All other types require a maturity_date.

current_value.description: Current market value; may be less than amount_invested

maturity_date.note: Null when investment_type='stocks'; required for all other types

returns_percentage.description: Can be negative for loss-making investments

relationships.description: Each employee belongs to one branch
Manager must work at this same branch — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Manager must work at this same branch — see data_integrity_rules

relationships.description: One customer can have multiple accounts
Denormalised — enforced equal to accounts.customer_id for this account
Must match the customer of cards.account_id — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Must match the customer of cards.account_id — see data_integrity_rules

relationships.description: Derived from transaction→account→customer chain — see data_integrity_rules
relationships.integrity_rule: Derived from transaction→account→customer chain — see data_integrity_rules

glossary.meaning: A person or business entity represented by a customer master record.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Query the 'customers' collection using 'customer_id' as the primary key.

glossary.meaning: Unique domain identifier linking customer profiles to accounts, loans, cards, and transactions.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Always join on domain key 'customer_id' (e.g. CUST000001), never MongoDB '_id'.

glossary.meaning: Process of verifying customer identity and regulatory documentation.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Check 'customers.kyc_status' on customer profile or query 'kyc_documents' for submitted documents.

glossary.meaning: Categorical state of KYC verification (e.g., 'verified', 'pending', 'rejected').
glossary.implementation_guidance: Stored as lowercase categorical string in 'customers.kyc_status'.

glossary.meaning: Identity or address proof record submitted by a customer (e.g. passport, driving licence, utility bill).
A customer who has completed identity verification successfully.
Customer risk classification assigned by risk assessment models (e.g., 'low', 'medium', 'high').
Customer categorized into the highest risk category.
System-generated flag identifying a suspicious transaction or unusual activity for review.
A transaction that triggered a fraud alert or has 'is_flagged' set to true.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Filter with { 'is_flagged': True } on 'transactions' or join with 'fraud_alerts'.

glossary.meaning: An alert reviewed and determined not to represent fraudulent behavior.
glossary.implementation_guidance: In 'fraud_alerts', status is 'closed' or 'dismissed'. Note: no explicit 'is_false_positive' boolean field exists in database.

glossary.meaning: Regulatory compliance processes designed to prevent illegally obtained funds from being disguised.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Relevant to transactions with high amounts or flagged status ('is_flagged') and customer risk category.

glossary.meaning: Deposit or current account held by a customer at a specific bank branch.
Current cleared funds available in the bank account.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Stored in 'accounts.balance' as a numeric field in INR.

glossary.meaning: Operational state of an account ('active', 'dormant', 'frozen', 'closed').
Individual financial debit or credit movement on an account.
Execution status of a transaction ('completed', 'failed', 'pending', 'reversed').
Timestamp when transaction took place. Stored as BSON Date object.
Commercial entity or merchant receiving payment in commercial transactions.
Industry classification of merchant (e.g., 'Groceries', 'Electronics', 'Healthcare', 'Dining').
Credit facility sanctioned to a customer with principal, interest, and repayment terms.
State of loan lifecycle ('active', 'closed', 'defaulted').
glossary.implementation_guidance: Stored as lowercase string in 'loans.status'. Integrity rules: 'closed' implies outstanding_amount=0; 'active' implies outstanding_amount>0.

glossary.meaning: Total remaining principal unpaid on a loan facility.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Mapped strictly to 'loans.outstanding_amount'. This is NOT overdue amount.

glossary.meaning: Payment amount past its scheduled due date and unpaid.
glossary.implementation_guidance: CRITICAL: 'overdue_amount' is NOT an existing field in the loans collection. Do not invent this field. Use 'loans.outstanding_amount' for total debt, or check next_due_date and status='defaulted'.

glossary.meaning: Number of days loan repayment has remained unpaid past due date.
glossary.implementation_guidance: CRITICAL: 'days_past_due' is NOT a field in the loans database. Do not hallucinate this field. Calculate relative to 'loans.next_due_date' if requested.

glossary.meaning: A loan classified as non-performing due to prolonged default.
glossary.implementation_guidance: In current dataset, defaulted loans are represented by { 'status': 'defaulted' } in the 'loans' collection.

glossary.meaning: The physical branch that approved and sanctioned the loan facility.
Physical bank location hosting accounts and sanctioning loans.
Unique branch identifier (e.g. BR00001).
glossary.implementation_guidance: Primary key for 'branches', referenced in 'accounts.branch_id', 'employees.branch_id', and 'loans.sanctioning_branch_id'.

glossary.meaning: Bank staff member assigned to a branch and department.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Collection 'employees'. Referenced as branch manager, account manager, loan officer, ticket agent, and KYC verifier.

glossary.meaning: Customer service request or complaint filed by a customer.
Payment card (debit or credit) issued to an account holder.
Wealth portfolio asset (mutual funds, fixed deposits, stocks, gold bonds).
Entities currently operational and in-service.
glossary.implementation_guidance: Filter with status = 'active' across accounts, loans, cards, customers, or branches.

glossary.meaning: A loan obligation that has not been serviced by its due date.
glossary.implementation_guidance: In this dataset, overdue/defaulted loans are represented by loans.status = 'defaulted' or next_due_date in the past. Do not use overdue_amount.
